newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries fall on weaker dollar in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries fall on weaker dollar in Tokyo.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were depressed by the dollar's fall against the yen by midday Tokyo on Wednesday after rising modestly overnight, traders said.
"The fall in the dollar after tankan weighed on Treasuries. But besides the dollar, the market is very quiet," a Japanese brokerage trader said.
The dollar was hammered down by strong buying of the yen in reaction to the stronger-than-expected figures in the Bank of Japan's "tankan" quarterly survey.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond was at 98-31/32, yielding 6.70 percent, compared with 99-4/32 in New York.
The diffusion index for major manufacturers, a key gauge of business confidence in the tankan, rose to plus seven in June from plus two in March, when the previous survey was conducted.
In reaction to the stronger-than-expected tankan results, Japanese interest rates rose across the board.
"The rise in Japanese interest rates has had no direct impact on Treasuries so far," the trader said. "But a further decline in the dollar could pressure Treasuries downwards."
Traders said the market was watching out for the outcome of a five-year note auction. The Treasury will sell $11.5 billion worth of the five-year note later today.

Traders said the Treasury market has fully recovered from the decline triggered by Japan Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's comments on Monday that Japan might be tempted to sell its holdings of U.S. Treasuries.

"No effect of the Hashimoto shock seen. It seems that the market used his comment as an excuse to sell Treasuries," a U.S. brokerage manager said. "Treasury prices still remain very expensive, especially in the shorter end."
The manager, however, said the market is likely to stay range-bound until next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting and U.S. jobs data.
The September T-bond futures contract fell 5/32 from the previous close to 112. It was moving in a range of 111-31/32 to 112-7/32.
